question: What is the primary causative organism of amoebiasis?
explanation: Entamoeba histolytica is the specific protozoan parasite responsible for causing amoebic infections and related complications in humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h1)

question: Why do many people infected with the parasite remain without any symptoms?

options.A: Stomach acid neutralizes the toxin production completely
options.B: The parasite only feeds on dietary waste products
options.C: Human immunity completely destroys the cysts before they hatch
options.D: The organism stays limited to the gut without invading tissue

explanation: Carriers often harbor luminal infection without tissue penetration, meaning they shed cysts without showing clinical signs of disease. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h1)

question: Which form of the parasite is responsible for surviving harsh environmental conditions outside the human body?
explanation: The tough outer wall of the cyst protects the parasite outside the host, allowing it to survive in water or soil. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h2)

question: How do houseflies contribute to the spread of amoebiasis in a community?

options.A: Breeding rapidly inside clean drinking water reservoirs
options.B: Injecting trophozoites directly into human skin during feeding
options.C: Spreading bacterial co-infections that activate dormant cysts
options.D: Carrying cysts mechanically from faeces to unprotected food

explanation: Insects act as mechanical vectors by landing on contaminated waste and then walking over food items meant for consumption. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h2)

question: What shape do sores or ulcers typically form in the large intestine during amoebiasis?
explanation: Trophozoites burrow into the intestinal lining, widening beneath the surface to create distinctive flask-shaped ulcerations. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h3)

question: A patient has lower abdominal pain, painful straining when passing stool, and bloody mucus in the stool. What condition is most likely present?
explanation: The classic signs of abdominal cramping, painful straining, and bloody mucous stools point directly toward invasive intestinal amoebiasis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h3)

question: Why are multiple stool samples often requested when checking for intestinal parasites?

options.A: Laboratories require large volumes for chemical blood tests
options.B: Parasite shedding in stool can be irregular and intermittent
options.C: Single samples are automatically destroyed by hospital policy
options.D: Preservatives in collection bottles dissolve the first sample

explanation: Collecting samples across consecutive days increases the chance of capturing cysts or trophozoites that are not constantly shed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h4)

question: Which diagnostic method is most reliable for identifying an amoebic liver abscess?

options.A: Direct visualization via a skin scratch test
options.D: Chest X-ray examination of the rib cage

explanation: Imaging modalities like ultrasound clearly reveal fluid-filled cavities and focal lesions inside the liver tissue. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h4)

question: Why must treatment for amoebiasis often include two different types of medications?

options.A: One drug kills tissue invaders while another clears cysts in the gut
options.B: Local guidelines forbid prescribing single-drug therapy for safety
options.C: Metronidazole alone causes immediate kidney failure in adults
options.D: Parasites develop resistance within twenty-four hours of treatment

explanation: A complete cure requires clearing both active trophozoites in the tissues and dormant cysts lingering in the gut lumen. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h5)

question: A patient with severe amoebic dysentery receives metronidazole. What essential nursing intervention supports this medical therapy?

options.A: Encouraging a high-fiber diet immediately to speed up bowel movement
options.B: Restricting all oral fluids to keep the inflamed colon resting
options.C: Monitoring fluid balance and assessing stool consistency closely
options.D: Isolating the patient in a private room with a surgical mask

explanation: Frequent dysenteric stools put patients at risk for dehydration, making intake and output monitoring vital for nursing care. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h5)

question: What is the most frequent extra-intestinal site affected by migrating amoebic trophozoites?
explanation: Trophozoites enter the mesenteric venules and travel straight to the liver through the portal circulation, forming abscesses. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h6)

question: How does an amoeboma sometimes complicate the clinical assessment of a patient?

options.A: It stops all digestive enzyme secretion permanently
options.B: It forms a mass that can be mistaken for bowel cancer
options.C: It turns the skin completely yellow due to sudden jaundice
options.D: It causes immediate paralysis of the lower extremities

explanation: Granulomatous tissue thickening in the colon can mimic a tumor mass during physical or radiographic examination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is the most effective way to prevent the transmission of amoebiasis in a community?

options.A: Ensuring safe drinking water and proper sanitation facilities
options.B: Administering yearly vaccines to all school-aged children
options.C: Screening every pregnant woman during antenatal visits
options.D: Banning the sale of locally grown fresh vegetables

explanation: Stopping fecal contamination of drinking water and food sources directly halts the transmission cycle of the parasite. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h7)

question: Why is washing raw fruits and vegetables an essential preventive practice against amoebiasis?

options.A: It removes parasite cysts deposited by contaminated water or handlers
options.B: It destroys the chemical pesticides sprayed during farming
options.C: It prevents flies from laying eggs inside the pulp
options.D: It activates natural enzymes that digest leftover bacteria

explanation: Fresh produce eaten raw can carry microscopic cysts if washed in dirty water or handled by infected persons. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h7)
